steps_h2: How to make product video ads
steps_lead: Shoot one clear photo, make the file, then post it.

steps.d: Put the product in daylight on a plain surface and take one sharp phone photo.
Upload the photo, pick a layout or describe the scene, and read the credit cost before you start.
Save the still or the clip, add text in your editor, and post it. Files can be used commercially and have no watermark.

faq.q: Do I need a camera or a studio?
faq.a: No. A phone photo in daylight is enough to start. The photo guide shows the setup.

faq.q: Which guide should I read first?
faq.a: If you do not have a clear photo yet, start with the phone-photo guide. If the photo is ready, open the guide for the job you are posting today.

faq.q: Do the guides quote live channel rules?
faq.a: They describe the rules sellers run into most often, such as a plain main image and the common frames. Check the channel's current help page before you launch, because those rules change.

faq.q: How much do the files in the guides cost?
faq.a: A clip is 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. The exact cost is shown before every job, and a failed job returns its credits.

faq.q: Can one source photo feed every guide?
faq.a: Yes, if the photo shows the whole item clearly. You can make a still from it and a clip from it. They are separate jobs.

faq.q: Can I add captions and music later?
faq.a: Yes. Add captions, a price, and licensed music after download. The tools do not burn captions into the file.

faq.q: Are the guides a substitute for the tool pages?
faq.a: No. A guide tells you how to do one job. The tool page is where you make the file. Use both.

faq.q: Can I follow these if I have never run an ad?
faq.a: Yes. The first-ad guide assumes you are starting from zero. It stops at a file you can upload. Your ad account setup stays in that channel's own help pages.
